sections.overview: Protoschinia scutosa is a noctuid moth found across warm parts of the Holarctic, with occasional records farther north.
sections.identification: It is a member of Noctuidae. Specialist moth accounts use both Protoschinia scutosa and Schinia scutosa for this species.
sections.habitat: It is associated with warm, dry habitats, including steppe-like areas with Artemisia.
sections.diet: The caterpillars feed mainly on Artemisia (mugworts and wormwoods), in the daisy family.
sections.behavior: Adults may fly in several generations from spring to autumn in parts of its range; timing varies with region and climate.
sections.reproduction: The reviewed sources describe the larval host plants but do not give a consistent species-wide account of egg laying or overwintering.
sections.ecology: Its caterpillars depend chiefly on mugworts and wormwoods, linking the moth to open, dry plant communities where these hosts grow.
sections.conservation: The sources consulted do not provide a global conservation assessment for this moth.
